Parameters, arguments and returns

Unit 1 · Week 5 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Python editor, badge_cost definition and a paper call-trace template.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Parameters, arguments and returns

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success means map arguments to parameters, use a return value and distinguish returned results from displayed output.

2. Retrieval: the first call

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and peer explanation

Expected badge_cost(4,3) returns 12. The body runs on a call. A caller can assign its returned result to cost. Allow individual retrieval then pair comparison. Retrace the call if learners think def immediately computes a numeric result.

3. Parameters and arguments

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked mapping and guided practice

Parameters width,height appear in def area(width,height). Arguments 5,2 appear in area(5,2). Positional binding maps first to first, second to second. Product 10 returns. Learners then map badge_cost(6,4): quantity 6, price 4, result 24. Support: align columns. Keyword and default arguments come later.

4. The caller can use the result

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher think-aloud and guided prediction

cost is 12, payable 14 and output 14. Trace entry into the function, return to assignment, then caller addition. Packaging is a separate caller calculation. Ask learners to predict badge_cost(2,5) plus 2:12. A result can be stored, displayed or combined.

5. Displaying and returning differ

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, run, investigate

This deliberately faulty calculation prints 12 inside the function, then caller prints None. Normal completion without an explicit return value returns None. Learners predict both lines, run and explain. Replace inner print with return quantity * unit_price. Corrected caller prints 12 once. A later numeric calculation needs a numeric returned result.

6. A result the caller can reuse

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired debugging with role changes

Repair print to return. Test (0,3)->0, (4,3)->12, (4,5)->20. The last result plus caller packaging 2 gives 22. Driver repairs while navigator traces the return, then swap. Input and printing stay outside. Support: annotate return-to-assignment. Stretch: explain how an extra print inside would add output without changing a numeric return.

7. What does the call return?

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student misconception check

Correct B: normal completion with no explicit return value gives None. Displaying 12 does not return 12. Take responses before discussion. If several choose A, assign a call result and inspect it separately. return ends that call; print displays output.

8. Exit ticket: map and use the values

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket

Parameters width,height receive arguments 7,2 and product 14 returns. Adding 3 in caller gives 17. Collect a labelled mapping and result. Revisit vocabulary or return/None according to errors.
